ECE 6390

Why a carrier creates sidebands

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows a 1 Hz message multiplied by an 8 Hz carrier, and the two 0.5 V spectral lines at 7 Hz and 9 Hz that the product contains.

Multiplying a message by a carrier translates its frequencies. For m(t) = cos(2πfₘt) and a carrier A_c·cos(2πf_c t), the product identity gives A_c·m(t)·cos(2πf_c t) = (A_c/2)cos[2π(f_c − fₘ)t] + (A_c/2)cos[2π(f_c + fₘ)t]: a lower sideband at f_c − fₘ and an upper sideband at f_c + fₘ, each of amplitude A_c/2.

A real message with content up to B hertz produces a band from f_c − B to f_c + B, so double-sideband modulation occupies 2B. The spectral cluster near −f_c is the conjugate mirror required for a real voltage; counting it again would double the bandwidth. The same product describes the receiver mixer, which multiplies by a local carrier to bring the band back down.

Variations change the lines. Double-sideband suppressed-carrier modulation puts all the power in the two sidebands. Conventional AM adds a constant before multiplying, which adds a carrier line at f_c that carries power but no information. Because each sideband of a real message carries the information of the other, single-sideband transmission keeps one and halves the occupied width to B.

Example

A 1 V carrier at 8 Hz multiplied by a 1 Hz unit-amplitude message gives cosines of 0.5 V at 7 Hz and 9 Hz. Into 1 Ω each carries 0.125 W, for 0.25 W in total, and the occupied width is 2 Hz. A message band up to 1 MHz on a 3 MHz carrier occupies 2 MHz to 4 MHz.

Practice

1. A message band from 0 to 4 kHz modulates a 1 MHz carrier in double-sideband form. Which RF band does it occupy, and how wide is it?

Each message frequency f appears at f_c ± f.

From 996 kHz to 1004 kHz, a width of 8 kHz, twice the message bandwidth.

2. Why does conventional AM use more transmitter power than double-sideband suppressed-carrier for the same sideband power?

Find the extra spectral line that the added constant creates.

The constant adds a carrier line at f_c. In the fully modulated single-tone case it carries twice the power of both sidebands together, yet it carries no message information.
